headline: This law gives legal backing to federal rules on how DEA registrations for controlled drugs can be changed, transferred, or ended.
what_it_does: Businesses and people who are registered with the federal government to make, sell, or hand out controlled substances need that registration to operate. The law sets out when a registration ends, including when the holder dies, stops existing as a legal entity, closes the business, or gives it up. It also sets notification requirements and conditions for transferring or assigning a registration to someone else.

who_it_affects.group: Pharmacies, doctors' offices, and other dispensers with federal controlled-substance registrations
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the rules for changing, transferring, or giving up their registration, including any notice requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Drug manufacturers and distributors registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration
who_it_affects.how: Their registrations end automatically in listed situations such as closing the business or ceasing legal existence, and transfers are allowed only under set conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Estates and heirs of registered individuals
who_it_affects.how: A registration ends when the registered person dies, so the estate or family must handle notice and wind-down under the rules.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on November 10, 2021; the official summary does not list a separate effective date.
